methodology: Aggressive dedup across 12 unit deep JSONs (~330 unit-level concept entries collapsed to 38 canonical CONCEPTs + 18 POSITIONs + 6 INVOLVEMENT-DIMENSIONs + 2 TEMPORAL-PHASEs). Tier-1 reserved for volume-pillar load-bearing concepts pervasive across ≥4 units. Tier-2 reserved for chapter-central concepts that are load-bearing within their home chapter and ramify into ≥2 others. Tier-3 reserved for supporting concepts that are load-bearing in only one chapter but rise to volume-relevance.

concepts.label: Player Involvement Model (PIM)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's volume-level frame: a 6-dimensional grid of involvement axes (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, affective, ludic) cross-cut by a macro/micro temporal-phase distinction, organized as layered and transparent rather than discrete.

concepts.label: Involvement (umbrella analytic)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The pre-immersive category of player engagement Calleja uses as the spine term — genus of which incorporation is the intensified species; analytic prerequisite to presence/immersion and itself resting on attention.

concepts.label: Incorporation
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's titular replacement frame: the most intensified and internalized blending of PIM dimensions, gated by a spatial+kinesthetic cornerstone and a simultaneity condition; structurally bidirectional (player absorbs the environment AND is absorbed into it); preserves both 'absorption' and 'transportation' senses of immersion in an expanded double-axis.

concepts.label: Macro temporal phase
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Off-line involvement with the game: pre-session and post-session thinking, planning, anticipation, community participation, motivation to return; the longer-term contextualization of the moment of gameplay.

concepts.label: Micro temporal phase (in ludo res)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: In-session, moment-to-moment engagement during the act of play; ergodically active in the dispositional sense; attentionally structured by the same six dimensions on a finer temporal grain.

concepts.label: Three-tier attentional hierarchy (attention → involvement → presence/immersion)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's stratification of player-experiential categories: attention is the precondition of involvement; involvement is the precondition of presence/immersion. The lower stratum must be modeled before the higher can be analyzed.

concepts.label: Family-resemblance methodology (Wittgensteinian)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's volume-level methodological signature, iteratively applied at three levels: at IG-01 to game-definition (vs. essentialism); at IG-03 to PIM dimensions as overlapping/non-essential axes; at IG-10 to incorporation as family-resemblance of experiential modes.

concepts.label: Virtual environment habitation
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The surviving spatial-phenomenological metaphor after the demolition of presence/immersion: the player's sense of inhabiting an on-screen place rather than perceiving a representation of space; the master metaphor of the spatial dimension and the load-bearing trope of the incorporation thesis.
synonyms_merged: metaphor of habitation grounded in everyday-life

concepts.label: Alterbiography (emergent player-narrative)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's term for the ongoing emergent autobiographical story of a player-character (or focalized entity / miniature) constituted through the player's interaction with the game world's embedded objects, inhabitants, and events; complement to (not opponent of) scripted narrative.

concepts.label: Ergodicity as dispositional readiness to act
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's reformulation of Aarseth's ergodic input: ergodic effort is first and foremost a dispositional readiness to act, not merely the physical pressing of buttons; cognitive effort and patient alertness count as ergodic.

concepts.label: Internalization (of attentional load / controls / space / shared involvement)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Process by which a learned task becomes automatic and ceases to consume the limited attentional resource, freeing capacity for other dimensions; paradigmatic at kinesthetic control-learning but operative for spatial place-internalization and shared involvement too.

concepts.label: Cybernetic circuit / cybernetic feedback loop
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Dovey + Kennedy 2006 figure for the player-machine loop: hardware + representational layer + rules + environment constitute a feedback circuit within which ergodic input takes effect; in IG-08 expanded to a cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic feedback loop.

concepts.label: Spatial+kinesthetic cornerstone of incorporation
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's gating condition for incorporation: spatial and kinesthetic involvement together are the necessary minimum substrate; without inhabited place and embodied control there is no incorporation. The kinesthetic→spatial dependency is the structural ground (you must move to inhabit).

concepts.label: Double-axis structure / bidirectional metaphor of incorporation
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Incorporation operates along two simultaneous axes: the player absorbs the virtual environment into consciousness AND the player's avatar is absorbed into the virtual environment. Replaces immersion's unidirectional plunge with a reversible bidirectional figure.

concepts.label: Simultaneity condition for incorporation
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The temporal-axis gate on incorporation: dimensions must operate at sustained intensity simultaneously (not serially); incorporation is sustainable-but-fleeting and its intensity is proportional to duration.

concepts.label: Experiential gestalts (Lakoff+Johnson via Calleja)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Lakoff+Johnson 2003 experientialist construct imported in IG-10 as the philosophical anchor for incorporation: metaphor is constitutive of cognition, not a deviation; experience is structured by holistic gestalts grounded in bodily lived-experience.

concepts.label: Subjective distance (player ↔ game environment)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The experiential variable the book theorizes: its shortening yields the sensation of inhabiting on-screen space. Proto-formulation of the bidirectional incorporation later articulated in IG-10.

concepts.label: Four conceptual challenges of presence/immersion
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's canonical enumeration in IG-02: (1) absorption-vs-transportation conflation; (2) ergodic-vs-non-ergodic media difference; (3) technological/fidelity determinism; (4) monolithic-perspective (immersion treated as single binary phenomenon). The destination Calleja's PIM and incorporation must answer.
synonyms_merged: C19 (IG-10) resolution of the four challenges

concepts.label: Avatar anchoring + system reactivity (structural differentia)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's structural specification of what makes game-environment presence different from non-game-media presence: the player is anchored via an avatar and the system reacts to player input in nontrivial, ergodic ways. The differentia that motivates a game-specific PIM.

concepts.label: Symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic control continuum
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: IG-04's primary typology of kinesthetic control mapping (Figure 4.3): symbolic (button-to-meaning, abstract); mimetic (gesture-replicates-action); symbiotic (player and game co-extended through internalized control). The chapter's load-bearing innovation in kinesthetic operationalization.

concepts.label: Agency (Murray/Schott vs. Giddens/capability)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's contested concept-bundle: Murray (1998) + Schott (2006) frame agency as satisfaction in seeing the result of one's decision; Calleja partially displaces this in favor of Giddens's agency-as-capability and Mateas+Stern's local/global agency. The chapter is the book's primary agency theorization.

concepts.label: Contingency (Malaby — performative + social)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Malaby 2007's claim that contingency is constitutive of games (not incidental); Calleja deploys it across IG-04 (contrivance of contingency / performance / risk-of-failure) and IG-06 (social contingency codependent on performative contingency).

concepts.label: Five-structure spatial taxonomy (Calleja)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's substitute for Nitsche's labyrinth/tracks-and-rails distinction: five spatial structures — unicursal corridor / labyrinth, multicursal corridor / maze, rhizomatic zone, open landscape, arena. Augmented by miniature and tactical spaces. The chapter's load-bearing typology.

concepts.label: Cognitive mapping / mental cartography
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Tolman 1948 via Golledge+Garling 2004: the player's construction of internal spatial models across nested scales (landmark + wayfinding + body-relative orientation + imageability). The cognitive substrate of spatial involvement.

concepts.label: Space → place transition (Tuan)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Tuan 1977's familiarization-yields-place schema, adopted by Calleja as the experiential mechanism by which navigable space becomes inhabited place — the spatial-internalization analog of kinesthetic-control-internalization.

concepts.label: MMOGs as third places / on-line societies
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: IG-06's central social-theoretic frame, importing Oldenburg's third-place concept via Steinkuehler + Williams: MMOGs are full-fledged on-line societies better at bridging than bonding social capital; governance, reputation, and persistent social bonds operate at MMOG scale.

concepts.label: Cohabitation / cooperation / competition (three-not-four shared subtypes)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's three modalities of shared involvement, including ambient awareness of social context. The 'three-not-four enumeration slip' surfaced in IG-06 as a notable internal-text inconsistency.

concepts.label: Human-vs-AI co-agent distinction
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: IG-06's position that player disposition is fundamentally restructured by perceived human-vs-AI status of co-agents — even rudimentary AI grounds cohabitation, but only persistent human-controlled agents support the reputation-and-betrayal layer (EVE Online Guiding Hand exemplar).
synonyms_merged: media equation / computers as social actors

concepts.label: Scripted narrative vs. alterbiography (co-constitutive)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's narrative-theoretic move that dissolves the narratology-vs-ludology binary: scripted narrative (designer-installed story-elements) and alterbiography (emergent player-narrative) are co-constitutive of narrative involvement, not mutually exclusive.

concepts.label: Push narrative vs. pull narrative
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's analytic distinction between designer-pushed scripted progression and player-pulled emergent-narrative pursuit — the dispositional reorientation that determines focalization and story-time/discourse-time interplay.

concepts.label: Excitatory homeostasis + rhetorical strategies of affect
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Bryant+Davies 2006 media-psychology frame, central to IG-08: affect is the emotional-tonal modulation of involvement generated via the cognitive+emotional+kinesthetic feedback loop, ranging across calming/adrenaline/uncanny. Designed and player-precipitated affect both count.

concepts.label: Escapism vs. escape (round-trip vs. one-way)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's defense of escapism via Tolkien (Escape of the Prisoner vs. Flight of the Deserter): escapism is a legitimate round-trip imaginative activity that returns to the everyday, distinct from one-way escape. Imagination is the human faculty enabling escapism; secondary worlds (Tolkien 1983) are its habitable form.
synonyms_merged: Escape of the Prisoner vs Flight of the Deserter

concepts.label: Strategy / tactics / microtactics three-tier hierarchy
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's IG-09 analytic innovation: strategies = plans in pursuit of primary goals; tactics = plans in pursuit of subgoals; microtactics = plans during moment of action. The three-tier hierarchy tracks goal-tier and temporal-distance and is the ludic dimension's load-bearing typology.

concepts.label: Goal-source taxonomy (system / self / community)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's three-way classification of goal-origin: game-stipulated, player-stipulated, community-stipulated. Refuses both Suits's lusory-attitude single-source goal-genesis and McIntosh's claim of universal primary-goal concreteness in games.

concepts.label: Magic-circle excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's deliberate exclusion of the Huizinga/Salen+Zimmerman/Juul magic-circle concept on two grounds: spatial redundancy (in digital games only navigable virtual space can be acted in) and empirical absence (no game-specific experiential bracketing in his interview data). One of three excisions structuring IG-03.
synonyms_merged: magic-circle critique applied to MMOG governance (C06 IG-06)

concepts.label: Lusory-attitude excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's refusal of Suits's lusory-attitude criterion (voluntary adoption of inefficient rule-restricted means) on two grounds: digital games enforce rules mechanically (no voluntary adoption needed) and Suits's argument is circular.

concepts.label: Fun-essentialism excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's rejection of the fun=games equation on two grounds: fun imposes a normative status that ignores variation across players' experiential states (including MMOG labor/tedium per Steinkuehler, Yee, Dibbell) and is analytically empty as a category.

concepts.label: Grounded-theoretic qualitative methodology (WoW + Planetside)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's three-year qualitative research design: extended personal participation in WoW (Blizzard 2004) and Planetside (SOE 2003), 25 in-game semi-structured interviews (two 2-hour sessions, in-game), focus groups, forum monitoring, blog tracking, machinima review; iterative coding generates the six dimensions as clusters of emphasis. The dissertation's empirical-adaptation seed.

dimensions.label: KINESTHETIC involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with avatar / game-piece control, spanning from conscious learning of the controls to fluent internalized movement; foregrounded when controls 'make themselves present' through unmastery or complex-sequence demand. The ergodic-dispositional substrate of the other dimensions.
dimensions.macro_signature: Recalling impressive feats of avatar control

dimensions.label: SPATIAL involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with spatial qualities of a virtual environment via spatial control, navigation, and exploration; the internalizing of game-space such that the player senses inhabiting a place rather than perceiving a representation of space.
dimensions.macro_signature: Spatial mental models maintained off-line (WoW Ratchet-to-Feathermoon route-planning)

dimensions.label: SHARED involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with awareness of and interaction with other agents (human- or computer-controlled) under modalities of cohabitation, cooperation, and competition; encompasses guild-political deliberation, ambient social-context awareness, and the human-vs-AI distinction.
dimensions.macro_signature: Clan-website work, guild-political deliberation, persisting social bonds

dimensions.label: NARRATIVE involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with both story-elements scripted into the game and emergent stories generated by ongoing interaction with the game world, its embedded objects, inhabitants, and events. Dissolves the narratology-vs-ludology binary via the scripted/alterbiography co-constitution.
dimensions.macro_signature: Speculation about designed-narrative development; story-construction featuring one's character
dimensions.micro_signature: In-session engagement with scripted + emergent story-elements; alterbiography-occurrence-locus

dimensions.label: AFFECTIVE involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with emotional states elicited by play — from calming aesthetic response through adrenaline-rush arousal to action-horror uncanny — including both designer-installed rhetorical strategies of affect and player-precipitated affective interpretations.
dimensions.macro_signature: Sense of inner peace after aesthetic travels; anticipatory excitement/anxiety about next session
dimensions.micro_signature: In-session calming/adrenaline/uncanny responses to designed + precipitated triggers
dimensions.primary_typology: C-031 (excitatory homeostasis + rhetorical strategies) + C-032 (escapism vs escape)
dimensions.note: Calleja flags this as substantively under-developed in IG-08 (shortest dimension chapter at 12 pp.)

dimensions.label: LUDIC involvement
dimensions.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with choices and their repercussions across game-stipulated, player-stipulated, and community-stipulated goals; opportunity cost is constitutive of well-balanced ludic systems — without repercussions, actions lose meaning.
dimensions.macro_signature: Winning-strategy formation; character-development planning; opportunity-cost rehearsal between sessions

positions.claim: Incorporation displaces immersion + presence as primary theoretical frame.
The shortening of subjective distance is not a stand-alone phenomenon but a blending of experiential phenomena; in its most intensified + internalized form it culminates in incorporation.
Digital-game involvement requires a dedicated theoretical apparatus — other-media perspectives are not irrelevant but require expansion and at times rethinking before they apply.
Involvement is the prior analytical category to presence and immersion; both higher-order phenomena rest on a well-modeled involvement substrate (which itself rests on attention).
Player experience is structured by two temporal phases — macro (off-line) and micro (in-session) — within each of which the six dimensions operate at distinct temporal grains.
The six dimensions are layered and transparent rather than discrete; one dimension changes the perception of the others without occluding them; inclusion/exclusion alters how the others operate.
Ergodicity is first and foremost a disposition / readiness to act, not the physical pressing of an input device; cognitive effort and patient alertness are equally ergodic.
The magic circle is redundant for digital games as a spatial marker and empirically unsupported as an experiential bracket; it is excluded from the model.
Fun is not the essence of play and is analytically empty; it imposes a normative status that obscures variation in experiential states (including MMOG labor / tedium).
Games are members of an extended family that share resemblances (Wittgensteinian) — not a set with a rigid essentialist definition (refuses Juul 2005 and Salen+Zimmerman 2003 essentialisms).

Virtual game environments — the intersection of the game-family and the virtual-environment-family — are the volume's unit of analysis (digitized card/puzzle games excluded; Half-Life 2 + WoW paradigmatic).
Habitation (not plunge) is the right metaphor; spatial+kinesthetic are the necessary minimum cornerstone of incorporation.

Virtual environments are continuous with media-saturated everyday life, not experientially separate otherworlds; subjective disposition (not merely medium acknowledgment) is required for incorporation.
Calleja DISSOLVES the narratology-vs-ludology binary by treating scripted-narrative and alterbiography as co-constitutive of narrative involvement.

Escapism is a legitimate, defensible cultural-imaginative round-trip activity — not a derogatory one-way escape — and the affective dimension is the volume's substantively under-developed dimension (not a description-deficit).
Rules constrain action AND enable meaning — restriction is constitutive of meaningfulness, not opposed to it; without repercussions, actions lose meaning.
The PIM is offered as a common holistic framework for further research — a first considered step toward eventual poststructural successor models, not a closed system.
WoW (Blizzard 2004) and Planetside (SOE 2003) are prototypical MMORPG/MMOFPS case-sites whose binary comparative scaffold is the volume's methodological backbone.

biggest_dedup_merges.note: involvement / player engagement / involvement-as-umbrella across nearly every unit
habitation / metaphorically-habitable-environment / place (Tuan) / virtual-environment habitation / inhabited place — spread across IG-00/02/05/10/11
ergodicity / ergodic effort / dispositional readiness / anticipatory readiness — Calleja's reformulation of Aarseth pervasive across IG-01/02/03/04/09
internalization / control internalization / 'Quan' / spatial internalization / shared-involvement internalization — Calleja's universal move applied to each dimension

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Anti-essentialist Wittgensteinian methodology vs. construction of a six-dimensional taxonomic apparatus
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: C-007 (family-resemblance) refuses essentialist necessary-and-sufficient conditions; C-001 (PIM) and the six dimensions then constitute a 6x2 grid that taxonomically organizes player experience. Calleja softens this via the 'layered + transparent' principle (P-006), but the formal structure remains taxonomic.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Metaphor-disclaimer vs. analytic-superiority claim about incorporation
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: Calleja simultaneously calls incorporation 'ultimately a metaphor like presence or immersion' (IG-00) and claims it provides 'a more robust concept' (IG-10). Robustness must therefore live in the metaphor's tracking of the multi-dimensional phenomenon, not in literal ontological gain — important for any project that wants to ground incorporation ontologically.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Bottom-up grounded-theoretic emergence vs. presentation as exhaustive taxonomy
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: Calleja states the six dimensions are clusters derived from interview data on two MMOG case-sites — implying revisability — but the chapter-architecture treats them as the complete inventory. Empirical-base / claim-scope asymmetry.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Macro vs. micro phase developmental asymmetry
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: Micro exposition dominates IG-03 and the dimension chapters; macro phase is comparatively thin and often appears as chapter-opening section. T-001 is under-theorized relative to T-002 across the volume.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Diagrammatic-structural vs. experiential-phenomenological registers of the PIM
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: The model is presented diagrammatically (Figure 3.1's wagon-wheel) but the underlying phenomenology is continuous, gradient, non-discrete. Diagrammatic and experiential registers pull against each other.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Generic 'affordances' usage without Gibson attribution (Phase 0 finding)
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: Calleja uses 'affordance' 11 times across the volume without citing Gibson — the Gibson-as-implicit-Uexküll-bridge hypothesis is falsified. The dissertation's Layer C must treat Uexküll mapping as singly-anchored anticipatory projection.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Three-not-four shared-modalities authorial enumeration slip
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: Internal-text inconsistency in IG-06's enumeration of shared modalities — cohabitation/cooperation/competition (3) where some passages imply 4. Worth flagging for the concept-matrix audit.

notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.label: Affective chapter's substantive under-development (acknowledged by Calleja)
notable_tensions_flagged_for_3B.summary: IG-08 is the volume's shortest dimension chapter (12 pp.) and Calleja flags it as substantively under-developed (P-015). The affective dimension is therefore the weakest link in the PIM's empirical-systematic exposition.
